Does not exist a formal National Open Data Strategy published yet. Since 2021, a project is underway for the National Data Strategy, (URL: https://portugaldigital.gov.pt/en/accelerating-digital-transition-in-portugal/get-to-know-the-digital-transition-strategies/national-data-strategy/). The document should be finshed until the end of 2022 but to our knowledge that was not accomplished.
Another project coordenated by the AMA (Administrative Modernization Agency) is in execution since August 2022 for the definition if the Data Strategy in the Public Administration (URL: not available); Both projects addresses open data as well. 
Other relevant informations are:
The Recovery and Resilience Plan (PRR) has a mission framework that also defines strategic objectives for open data. (URL: https://recuperarportugal.gov.pt/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/PRR.pdf). In addition to these references, there are others; that are also related to open data: 1 - In regards to public open data, the strategy is embedded in our ICT government strategy, as an enabler of innovation and competitiveness, with measures including: the extension of the open data disclosure and use via the national data portal; the disclosure of execution indicators and benefits accomplished by executing public administration policies, initiatives and projects; and, the provision of instruments that facilitate the participation of citizen in public decision processes. 2 - It is part of the National Strategy for AI to guarantee an ethical-by-design AI, where open data plays a relevant role. The National Data Strategy is a finalized document that was supposed to be published by the end of 2023. However, due to political changes, the caretaker government postponed its publication. The new executive is expected to publish it within the next few months. This strategy (document attached to the survey with the name "Estratégia Nacional de Dados_20231219_v1.0.pdf") aims to ensure that Portugal is one of the pioneering countries participating in the European data ecosystem, thus enhancing its value, creating new services and products both in Portugal and beyond its borders.
The National Data Strategy provides continuity and strengthen national open data initiatives and the re-use of public sector information, whose general principles are approved in Law No. 68/2021 (already rectified by Rectification Declaration No. 31/2021), which in turn transposes into national law Directive (EU) 2019/1024 of 20 June 2019. column2:
Does the national strategy/policy include an action plan with measures to be implemented in the open data field?

For Explanation:
If yes, please briefly describe the main measures described by the action plan.
column4:
By the Law No. 68/2021. Examples: The entities covered must ensure the publication of available documents and data, inventories of accessible documents and related metadata, as well as search possibilities, under the terms of the regime of access to administrative and environmental information and the reuse of administrative documents. The data.gov portal is the central catalog of open data in Portugal, with the function of aggregating, referencing, publishing and hosting open data from different bodies and sectors of Central, Regional and Local Public Administration, also functioning as an indexing portal, of content hosted on other open, sectoral or decentralized data portals or catalogs:
• The open data made available therein must maintain levels of updating and permanent quality, so that they can be reliably reused by other computer applications;
• If the entity producing the open data does not make them accessible from its own systems, it must make them available on the data.gov portal, and must also ensure that they are always updated there. The related metadata must always be made available in an updated form to the data.gov portal, in order to facilitate their search and location as open data, including in cases where the entity producing the open data makes them accessible from of own systems; etc.
The  concrete action/measures planned for the fulfilling of those obligation are laid down in the document "Plano de Ação Transversal para a Transformação Digital da AP 2021-2023"  (https://tic.gov.pt/documentos/plano-de-acao-para-a-transformacao-digital-da-ap-2021-2023), which corresponds to the Action Plan for "Estratégia de Transformação Digital da AP 2021-2023" (https://tic.gov.pt/estrategias/estrategia-2021-2026), Action 2 comprehends several measures relating to the open data filed.

column4: Of common scope to some of the strategies/policies, it is referred: The creation of infrastructures to support the consumption of data in real-time on the open data national portal; The identification of services that produce and optimize the consumption of data in real-time; The increase of real-time datasets on the national open data portal. One of "CTIC TIC 2021-2023-2026 Strategy" key goals is a single, integrated system allowing to enrich operational databases with geolocation, cartographic, socio-economic, populational, meteorological information, and points of interest. Real-time updates with smart business information and analysis tools. In the Simplex program, it is referred the following measures that feature real-time data: Measure # 119 Work Suitability Form with a model that will allow obtaining statistical indicators, in real-time, of anonymized (aggregated) data on work capacity by sector of activity, profession, geographic area, gender, among others; Measure # 144 Single Agriculture Portal that aims to promote the simplification and streamlining of the relationship with farmers, citizens, companies and other economic agents, functioning as an online service point, with progressive availability of all information and services provided by the bodies of the Governmental Area of
column7: The National Data Strategy envisages a governance model that includes the development of a collaborative and dynamic ecosystem that enhances data altruism and the creation of value synergies between the various stakeholders. In this sense, the strategic pillar “Governance” materializes in a set of three strategic objectives: 1) the establishment of solid guidelines for the ethical and efficient management of data, promoting their reliability and security throughout their life cycle; 2)effective collaboration between stakeholders, encouraging the exchange of data and resources in a mutually beneficial way to drive innovation and value creation; 3)continuous monitoring and monitoring of the progress of data-related actions, using models to assess the impact that the initiatives proposed in the strategy have on society and the economy.

column2:
Does the national strategy/policy outline measures to incentivise the publication of and access to citizen-generated data?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please briefly describe the measures.
column7:
Law 68/2021 , which replaces law 26/2016, approves the general principles on open data and transposes Directive (EU) 2019/1024 of the European Parliament and of the Council, of 20 June 2019, on open data and the reuse of public sector information and states that any singular person who possesses information can publish and access data via the national open data portal. 
Also, one of the 4 pillars of its first Open Administration National Action Plan (URL: https://ogp.eportugal.gov.pt/monitorizacao) is precisely open data. OGP Portugal aims to guarantee concrete commitments from governments to promote transparency, encourage public participation, fight corruption, and use new technologies to strengthen participatory democracy - https://ogp.eportugal.gov.pt/inicio. 
In December of 2022, following the pillars of the second Open Administration National Action Plan 2022 (URL: https://ogp.eportugal.gov.pt/ii-panaa), AMA launched the Mosaico platform (URL: https://mosaico.gov.pt/), which promotes universal access to information between the state and the citizen. 
The third Open Administration National Action Plan (2024-27) is now underway (URL: https://ogp.eportugal.gov.pt/iii-panna)

Besides OGP, other examples are:
Despite the fact that there is not yet a formally approved strategy for open data (https://portugaldigital.gov.pt/en/accelerating-digital-transition-in-portugal/get-to-know-the-digital-transition-strategies/national-data-strategy/; https://www.incode2030.gov.pt/dados-abertos/), open data and data reuse are set as priorities for Portugal. In the Transversal Action Plan for Public Administration Digital Transformation (which contains transversal actions contributing for the implementation of the Strategy for Public Administration Digital Transformation 2021-2026), it is set up as transversal measure (https://tic.gov.pt/estrategias/plano-de-acao-transversal/valorizacao-dados-acao-transversal). It is emphasized that data literacy capacity building is crucial, as well as a great focus on inclusion and digital literacy. This is consistent with the Open Data Guide, in which there is a clear outline of the advantages for open data for different users and the emphasis on the importance of establishing an open data ecosystem that involves various stakeholders (examples below) in the process of open data and reuse (https://www.ama.gov.pt/documents/24077/24804/guia_dados_abertos_ama.pdf/aa97d8e8-c5fe-47ab-9500-734948c02b19, especially pages 7-8 and 23).
An important example of establishing an open data ecosystem that involves various stakeholders, namely citizens, is citizen science projects. Several entities foster these data ecosystems to provide services to the community and contribute to science. Examples of such projects are: IPMA (https://www.ipma.pt/) and CIIMAR (https://www.ciimar.up.pt/), which have a project for monitoring jellyfish on the Portuguese coast, GelAvista (https://www.cienciacidada.pt/project/15); the RadAR project (https://eu-citizen.science/project/467), in which three Portuguese schools participate in an international effort to reduce indoor radon exposure; and CCMAR (https://ccmar.ualg.pt/en/our-strategy), which has several projects for citizen data sharing related to the marine environment (https://ccmar.ualg.pt/en/citizen-science). Several others can be found on this site: https://www.cienciacidada.pt/projects.
1) Arquivo.pt, which promotes an annual contest for innovative works based on open data (preserved by Arquivo.pt). Arquivo.pt is developed by the Scientific Computing Unit of FCT - Foundation for Science and Technology - https://sobre.arquivo.pt/pt/colabore/premios-arquivo-pt/premio-arquivo-pt-2024/. 
2) The Urban Co-Creation Data Lab project aims to support decision-making at the city level regarding high-quality services for citizens. The project is a collaboration between the Portuguese government (AMA) and NOVA IMS University. The project supports new planning and management approaches with new tools to evaluate the impact and predict various service demands (URL: https://www.urbandatalab.pt/). 
3) The DSPA represents the Data Science sector and promotes data science in Portugal and internationally. The association also promotes regulation, ethics, and security in the field of data science. It shares experiences, innovations, case-studies, and success stories and promotes innovation and entrepreneurship of Portuguese companies (URL: https://dspa.pt/)

dados.gov.pt is the Portuguese Public Administration’s open data portal. Its function is to aggregate, reference and host open data from different bodies and sectors of Public Administration, constituting the central catalog of open data in Portugal. In addition to functioning as a shared data hosting and publishing service, which can be used by any public body, it also functions as an indexing portal for content hosted on other open data portals/catalogs, whether sectoral (e.g. Health, Justice, Environment ) or local (e.g. Lisbon City Council, Águeda City Council). It also promotes cases of reuse that use public shared data, and provides varied information on the movement of open data, publication and reuse of data, among others.
Example 1: Lisbon City Council (Lisboa Aberta, URL: https://lisboaaberta.cm-lisboa.pt/index.php/pt/dados/estrategia-de-dados-abertos). Example 2: Porto City Council (URL:https://www.portodigital.pt/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/Plano-de-Gestão-e-Valorização-de-Dados-do-Município-do-Porto-_VFinal.pdf); etc.

column7:
The national open data portal, dados.gov, a dashboard updates the number of publications of re-uses and their temporal evolution.
A monitoring improved dashboard is also being designed to be published at the national open data portal (dados.gov), with indicators of entities' activity regarding open data (for example, the degree of compliance with the Law regarding High-Value Datasets). This dashboard is expected to be operational and launched soon.

#Reply following the questions of the research team:
The progress of public administration policies for digital transformation, particularly for open data initiatives, is evaluated annually based on the monitoring indicators defined and published in specific reports (https://www.ama.gov.pt/web/agencia-para-a-modernizacao-administrativa/quar). The attached document (Monitorização - QUAR - PA2023 - Após revisão.xlsx) contains the results for 2023. Since these indicators are quantitative and downstream of the Open Data measures, they tend to reflect the numerical evolution of the dados.gov portal, as defined in documents Ref.ª 33 and 59 (see column D).

The National Data Strategy focuses as well on empowering people, contributing to a more inclusive, informed society equipped with concrete tools (legislative and practical) to understand, critically evaluate and use data in a conscious and safe way, promoting an environment conducive to active participation in the digital era. 
The Agency for Administrative Modernization (AMA) is mandated to establish and maintain the national open data portal dados.pt. This also include providing assistance to data holders in publishing their data as an open data on the national portal. Also, the CTIC appointed a task force dedicated to data subjects including open data. This task force (TF) includes various public public sector bodies responsibles for open data. Also, the national open data portal Dados.gov makes available a tutotial on how to publish open data on the portal - https://dados.gov.pt/pt/pages/api-tutorial/
